question:
Which of the following pairs of 'disease – duration' is correct?
I. Acute – long duration
II. Chronic – short time
solution_text:
The correct answer is Neither I nor II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An acute disease develops suddenly and lasts for a short duration (days to a few weeks) — e.g., common cold, flu, chickenpox. (तीव्र रोग — अल्पकालिक)

 

• A chronic disease develops slowly and persists for a long duration, often months, years, or a lifetime — e.g., diabetes, arthritis, tuberculosis.

 

• Statement I calls Acute disease 'long duration', which is incorrect — acute diseases are short-term.

 

• Statement II calls Chronic disease 'short time', which is also incorrect — chronic diseases are long-term.

 

• Since both given statements reverse the actual definitions, neither is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diseases are broadly classified as communicable (infectious, caused by pathogens) and non-communicable (non-infectious, like most chronic lifestyle diseases).

 

• Some diseases can start acute and become chronic if untreated, such as hepatitis B or certain kidney conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Only II (Option 1): This would be correct only if Chronic meant short duration, which is factually wrong.

 

• Only I (Option 3): This would be correct only if Acute meant long duration, which is factually wrong.

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Since both statements reverse the true meanings of acute and chronic, this option is incorrect.

question: Which village in Gujarat was declared as the first round-the-clock solar powered village in India in October 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Modhera.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Modhera, a village in Mehsana district, Gujarat, famous for the Sun Temple, was declared India's first round-the-clock solar-powered village in October 2022. (मोढेरा — सूर्य मंदिर के लिए प्रसिद्ध गांव)

 

• Prime Minister Narendra Modi dedicated the Modhera Solar Village project to the nation on 9 October 2022, developed by combining rooftop solar panels with a battery energy storage system and a ground-mounted solar power plant.

 

• The project includes over 1,300 rooftop solar installations and a grid-connected solar power plant at Sujanpura, implemented with support from the Gujarat government.

 

• The choice of Modhera also carries symbolic significance, as the ancient Modhera Sun Temple is dedicated to the Sun God, Surya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Modhera Sun Temple was built in 1026–27 CE by King Bhima I of the Solanki (Chalukya) dynasty.

 

• India's push for solar villages is part of its broader renewable energy targets, including the goal of reaching 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.

 

NOTE

 

• Unai (Option 1): A town in Navsari district, Gujarat, known for its hot water springs, not a solar village.

 

• Waghai (Option 2): A town in Dang district, Gujarat, known for its botanical gardens and forests.

 

• Khavda (Option 3): A village in Kutch district, Gujarat, site of a large under-construction renewable energy park, but not the village declared India's first 24x7 solar-powered village.

question: Where does the East Coast of India lie?
option_1: Between Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal
option_4: Between Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin
solution_text:
The correct answer is Between Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's East Coast stretches along the eastern seaboard from West Bengal to Tamil Nadu and lies between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal. (पूर्वी तट — पूर्वी घाट और बंगाल की खाड़ी के बीच)

 

• It is a broader, emergent coastline compared to the West Coast and includes deltas of major rivers such as the Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi, and Kaveri.

 

• The East Coast is subdivided into the Coromandel Coast (Tamil Nadu–Andhra Pradesh, south) and the Northern Circars/Utkal Coast (Andhra Pradesh–Odisha, north).

 

• Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Pulicat Lake (Andhra Pradesh–Tamil Nadu) are notable lagoons along this coast.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The West Coast of India lies between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, running from Gujarat to Kerala.

 

• The East Coast is a plain of marine deposition, while much of the West Coast is a submerged coastline, making it narrower with natural harbours.

 

NOTE

 

• Between Maharashtra and Kerala (Option 2): This describes a stretch of the West Coast, not the East Coast.

 

• Between Diu and Kerala (Option 3): This roughly traces part of the West Coast of India, bordering the Arabian Sea.

 

• Between Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin (Option 4): This also describes the West Coast, running from Gujarat's Gulf of Khambhat down to Kanyakumari (Cape Comorin).

question: Which of the following sports was NOT played at Tokyo Olympics 2020 held in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021 due to COVID-19) featured 33 sports, including newly added disciplines like Surfing, Skateboarding, Sport Climbing, and Karate. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020)

 

• Cricket was not part of the Olympic programme at Tokyo 2020; it last featured in the Olympics in 1900 (Paris) and is approved to return only at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

 

• Shooting and Swimming are traditional, long-standing Olympic sports and were both contested at Tokyo 2020.

 

• Surfing made its Olympic debut at the Tokyo 2020 Games.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's best-ever Olympic performance came at Tokyo 2020, with Neeraj Chopra winning gold in javelin throw — India's first individual Olympic gold in athletics.

 

• Cricket will return to the Olympics after 128 years, at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, in the T20 format.

 

NOTE

 

• Shooting (Option 2): A regular Olympic sport since 1896 (with a few exceptions); India's shooters competed at Tokyo 2020.

 

• Swimming (Option 3): One of the core disciplines of the modern Olympics since 1896.

 

• Surfing (Option 4): A new sport added to the Olympic programme, making its debut at the Tokyo 2020 Games.

question: ______ serves as the entry and exit point of a network, as all data coming in or going out of a network must first pass through it in order to use routing paths.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gateway.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Gateway serves as the entry and exit point of a network; all data entering or leaving a network must pass through it to use the appropriate routing paths. (गेटवे — नेटवर्क का प्रवेश और निकास बिंदु)

 

• It acts as a node that connects two networks using different protocols, translating data formats so devices on separate networks can communicate.

 

• A home router often functions as a gateway, connecting a local network (LAN) to the wider Internet (WAN).

 

• Gateways can operate at higher layers (up to Layer 7) of the OSI model, unlike simpler devices such as repeaters or bridges.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A default gateway is the IP address a device sends traffic to when the destination is outside its local subnet.

 

• Gateways are essential for protocol conversion, e.g., connecting a TCP/IP network to a non-TCP/IP network.

 

NOTE

 

• Bridge (Option 2): Connects and filters traffic between two segments of the same network at the Data Link layer; it is not defined as the network's overall entry/exit point.

 

• Repeater (Option 3): Regenerates and amplifies signals to extend the range of a network, operating at the Physical layer.

 

• Router (Option 4): Directs data packets between different networks based on IP addresses, but it is the term 'Gateway' that is specifically defined here as the network's entry/exit point.

question: Which is the most important festival of Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bihu is the most important and widely celebrated festival of Assam, marking the Assamese New Year and agricultural cycles. (बिहू — असम का प्रमुख त्यौहार)

 

• There are three Bihus celebrated in a year: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (April, spring, New Year), Kongali/Kati Bihu (October, austere), and Bhogali/Magh Bihu (January, harvest).

 

• Bihu is celebrated with traditional Bihu dance and songs, accompanied by instruments like the dhol, pepa, and gogona.

 

• It is deeply tied to Assam's agrarian society, celebrating the sowing and harvesting of crops.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rongali Bihu (mid-April) is the most festive and widely celebrated of the three, coinciding with the Assamese New Year.

 

• Bihu dance has been performed at international platforms and holds cultural significance in showcasing Assamese identity.

 

NOTE

 

• Hornbill Festival (Option 1): A major festival of Nagaland, celebrated in December, showcasing Naga tribal culture.

 

• Lumbini Festival (Option 2): Associated with Lumbini, Nepal, the birthplace of Gautam Buddha; not an Assamese festival.

 

• Phool Dei (Option 4): A spring harvest festival celebrated in Uttarakhand, not Assam.

question: By which of the following process can we separate two miscible liquids?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Distillation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Distillation is used to separate two miscible liquids that have different boiling points, by heating the mixture and condensing the vapours. (आसवन — मिश्रणीय द्रवों को अलग करने की विधि)

 

• The liquid with the lower boiling point vaporizes first, is condensed separately, and collected, leaving behind the other liquid.

 

• A common example is separating a mixture of water and alcohol (ethanol), or purifying water containing dissolved salts, using simple distillation.

 

• For liquids with close boiling points, fractional distillation (using a fractionating column) is used instead, e.g., in refining crude petroleum.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Distillation is widely used industrially, including in petroleum refining, alcohol production, and desalination.

 

• Sublimation and crystallisation are used mainly for solid-liquid or solid-solid separations, not for two miscible liquids.

 

NOTE

 

• Crystallisation (Option 1): Used to obtain pure solid substances from a solution by controlled cooling/evaporation, e.g., purifying salt or sugar from an impure sample.

 

• Sublimation (Option 2): Separates a solid that directly changes to gas (e.g., camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride) from a mixture of solids.

 

• Chromatography (Option 4): Used to separate the components of a mixture (often dissolved in a solvent) based on differing rates of movement through a medium, commonly used for dyes/pigments — not the standard method for separating two miscible liquids.

question: Who is the first athlete to represent India in fencing at Tokyo Olympics 2020 held in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhavani Devi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• C.A. Bhavani Devi became the first Indian fencer to qualify for and compete at the Olympic Games, representing India in the sabre event at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021). (भवानी देवी — ओलंपिक में भाग लेने वाली पहली भारतीय तलवारबाज)

 

• She hails from Chennai, Tamil Nadu, and won her first-round bout against Tunisia's Nadia Ben Azizi before losing in the round of 32.

 

• Her participation was a historic milestone for Indian fencing, a sport with very limited representation from India internationally.

 

• She had previously won gold at the Tournoi Satellite fencing tournament in Iceland (2019), becoming the first Indian fencer to win an international medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fencing has three disciplines — foil, épée, and sabre — and Bhavani Devi competes in sabre.

 

• India's overall medal tally at Tokyo 2020 was 7 medals, its best-ever Olympic performance.

 

NOTE

 

• P.V. Sindhu (Option 2): Indian badminton player who won bronze at Tokyo 2020 (and silver at Rio 2016); not associated with fencing.

 

• PT Usha (Option 3): Legendary Indian sprinter from the 1980s, famous for narrowly missing an Olympic medal at the 1984 Los Angeles Games (400m hurdles); not a fencer.

 

• Aditi Ashok (Option 4): Indian golfer who narrowly missed a medal (finished 4th) at Tokyo Olympics 2020; not associated with fencing.

question: Mita performs "Ghoomar" at her school's annual function. Which state does this dance form originate from?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ghoomar is a traditional folk dance that originates from Rajasthan, performed mainly by women dressed in colourful ghagra-choli, swirling in circular movements. (घूमर — राजस्थान का लोक नृत्य)

 

• It is traditionally performed on festive occasions such as weddings, Teej, and other auspicious functions, originating among the Bhil tribe and later widely adopted by Rajput communities.

 

• The dance is characterised by graceful, swaying movements of the ghagra (long skirt) as dancers twirl gracefully in circles.

 

• Ghoomar gained wider popular recognition after being featured prominently in Bollywood films set in Rajasthan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ghoomar is recognised as one of the traditional dance forms representative of Rajasthani culture and is often performed at state and national cultural events.

 

• Other Rajasthani folk dances include Kalbelia, Chari, and Kachhi Ghodi.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Garba and Dandiya Raas, not Ghoomar.

 

• Punjab (Option 2): Known for Bhangra and Giddha, not Ghoomar.

 

• Odisha (Option 3): Known for the classical dance Odissi and folk dances like Chhau, not Ghoomar.

question: Law of Demand states that, there is a negative relationship between ______.
option_1: demand for a commodity and its supply
option_2: supply of a commodity and its price
option_3: tax on a commodity and its price
option_4: demand for a commodity and its price
solution_text:
The correct answer is demand for a commodity and its price.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Law of Demand states that, all else being equal (ceteris paribus), there is an inverse (negative) relationship between the price of a commodity and the quantity demanded of it. (मांग का नियम — कीमत और मांग में व्युत्क्रम संबंध)

 

• As the price of a commodity rises, the quantity demanded falls, and as the price falls, the quantity demanded rises — represented by a downward-sloping demand curve.

 

• This relationship holds under the assumption that income, tastes/preferences, and prices of related goods remain constant.

 

• Exceptions to the Law of Demand include Giffen goods and Veblen goods, where demand may not fall despite a price rise.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Law of Demand is a foundational principle of Neoclassical economics, closely associated with Alfred Marshall's demand theory.

 

• The Law of Supply, in contrast, shows a positive/direct relationship between price and quantity supplied.

 

NOTE

 

• Demand for a commodity and its supply (Option 1): Demand and supply are jointly determined at equilibrium, but the Law of Demand specifically concerns price and quantity demanded, not supply directly.

 

• Supply of a commodity and its price (Option 2): This describes the Law of Supply, which shows a positive relationship, not the Law of Demand.

 

• Tax on a commodity and its price (Option 3): A tax generally increases the price of a commodity (a positive relationship); this is not what the Law of Demand describes.

question: Which law is also known as the law of inertia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newton's First law of motion.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's First Law of Motion, also called the Law of Inertia, states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion continues in uniform motion in a straight line, unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force. (न्यूटन का प्रथम नियम — जड़त्व का नियम)

 

• Inertia is the inherent property of matter that resists any change in its state of rest or uniform motion.

 

• This principle was first conceptualised by Galileo Galilei and later formalised by Sir Isaac Newton in his work *Principia Mathematica* (1687).

 

• A classic example: passengers jerk forward when a moving bus suddenly stops, due to their body's inertia of motion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Newton's Second Law relates force, mass, and acceleration (F = ma).

 

• Newton's Third Law states that every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

 

NOTE

 

• Archimedes principle (Option 1): States that a body submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of fluid displaced; unrelated to inertia.

 

• Newton's Second law of motion (Option 3): Defines force as the rate of change of momentum (F = ma); it is not called the law of inertia.

 

• Kepler's law (Option 4): A set of three laws describing the motion of planets around the Sun; unrelated to inertia.

question: Which part of the Indian Constitution is related with the Fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) deals with Fundamental Rights, often called the 'Magna Carta' of India. (भाग III — मौलिक अधिकार)

 

• It originally guaranteed six fundamental rights; after the 44th Amendment (1978), the Right to Property was removed, leaving six rights: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies.

 

• These rights are justiciable, meaning citizens can approach the Supreme Court (Article 32) or High Courts (Article 226) directly for their enforcement.

 

• Fundamental Rights are inspired by the Bill of Rights of the US Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part IV of the Constitution deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are non-justiciable.

 

• Part IV-A (Article 51A) deals with Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 

NOTE

 

• II (Option 1): Part II of the Constitution deals with Citizenship (Articles 5–11).

 

• IV (Option 2): Part IV deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy, not Fundamental Rights.

 

• I (Option 4): Part I of the Constitution deals with the Union and its Territory (Articles 1–4).

question: In September 2022, which state bagged the international tourism award for “Best destination for culture”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is West Bengal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, West Bengal won the ‘Best Destination for Culture’ award, conferred by a forum of international travel writers/journalists. (पश्चिम बंगाल — सर्वश्रेष्ठ सांस्कृतिक गंतव्य पुरस्कार)

 

• The award recognised West Bengal's rich cultural heritage, including its festivals (like Durga Puja), historical sites, and artistic traditions.

 

• The recognition came around the same period the state was actively promoting Durga Puja, which was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2021.

 

• The award was received on behalf of the West Bengal Tourism Department at the ceremony.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kolkata (West Bengal) is often called the 'City of Joy' and is known for its colonial architecture, literature, and art.

 

• West Bengal's Durga Puja festival draws international recognition for its scale and artistic pandal designs.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala (Option 2): Known as 'God's Own Country', famous for backwaters and Ayurveda tourism, but not the recipient of this particular September 2022 award.

 

• Gujarat (Option 3): Known for tourist destinations like the Rann of Kutch and Statue of Unity, but not this particular award.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 4): Home to the Taj Mahal and other heritage sites, but not the state honoured with this award in September 2022.

question: If ex ante aggregate demand and ex ante aggregate supply are plotted together in a graphical diagram, then at which point equilibrium will be reached?
option_1: Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply
option_2: Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero
option_3: Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply
option_4: Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply
solution_text:
The correct answer is Where ex ante aggregate demand is equal to ex ante aggregate supply.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ex ante refers to the planned or intended values of a variable, as opposed to ex post, which refers to actual/realised values. (एक्स-एंटे — नियोजित मूल्य)

 

• Macroeconomic equilibrium in the goods market is reached at the point where ex ante (planned) Aggregate Demand equals ex ante (planned) Aggregate Supply.

 

• At this equilibrium point, there is no unplanned change in inventories, meaning producers' planned output exactly matches the planned expenditure by buyers.

 

• If ex ante AD exceeds ex ante AS, inventories fall unexpectedly, prompting producers to raise output; if ex ante AD is less than ex ante AS, inventories rise, prompting producers to cut output — in both cases the economy moves toward the equilibrium point.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• This concept underlies the Keynesian income-determination model, where equilibrium national income is determined by the intersection of the AD and AS curves.

 

• Aggregate Demand comprises consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports (C + I + G + (X−M)).

 

NOTE

 

• Where ex ante aggregate demand is zero (Option 2): Equilibrium is not defined by AD being zero; it is defined by AD equalling AS.

 

• Where ex ante aggregate demand is less than ex ante aggregate supply (Option 3): This represents a state of disequilibrium (excess supply/unplanned inventory build-up), not equilibrium.

 

• Where ex ante aggregate demand is more than ex ante aggregate supply (Option 4): This also represents disequilibrium (excess demand/unplanned inventory depletion), not equilibrium.

question: The concept of “Procedure Established by Law” in the Indian constitution is borrowed from which of the following countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Japan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The concept of ‘Procedure Established by Law’, enshrined in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, was borrowed from the Constitution of Japan. (कानून द्वारा स्थापित प्रक्रिया — जापान से ग्रहण)

 

• Under this doctrine, a person's life or personal liberty can be deprived only through a procedure laid down by a validly enacted law, without necessarily testing whether that law is fair or just.

 

• This is in contrast to 'Due Process of Law' (found in the US Constitution), which allows courts to examine both the substance/fairness and procedure of a law.

 

• Over time, through judicial interpretation (notably the Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India, 1978 case), the Indian judiciary has read elements of 'due process' into Article 21, requiring that the procedure be fair, just, and reasonable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Constitution borrows features from many countries: Parliamentary system (Britain), Fundamental Rights (USA), DPSP (Ireland), Federal structure (Canada), among others.

 

• Article 21 states: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.'

 

NOTE

 

• Britain (Option 1): India borrowed the parliamentary form of government, rule of law, and legislative procedures from Britain, but not 'Procedure Established by Law'.

 

• France (Option 2): India borrowed the ideals of Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity (Republic concept) from France.

 

• United States of America (Option 4): India borrowed Fundamental Rights, judicial review, and (partly, through judicial interpretation) the 'Due Process of Law' concept from the USA — but the original textual phrase 'Procedure Established by Law' itself comes from Japan.

question: What is the theme of “Digital India Week 2022”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Catalyzing New India’s Techade.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Digital India Week 2022 was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 4 July 2022 at Mahatma Mandir, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, with the theme ‘Catalyzing New India’s Techade’. (डिजिटल इंडिया सप्ताह 2022 — नए भारत के ‘टेकेड’ को गति देना)

 

• The event marked the ongoing progress of the Digital India initiative, launched in 2015, and showcased emerging technologies and digital government services.

 

• During the event, PM Modi launched several initiatives including Digital India Bhashini (AI-led language translation), Digital India GENESIS (National Centre of Excellence for startups), MyScheme (a platform for citizens to check scheme eligibility), and the Chip to Startup (C2S) programme.

 

• 'Techade' refers to India's vision of the 2020s as a decade of technology-led growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015 with the vision of transforming India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy.

 

• Key pillars of Digital India include digital infrastructure, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens.

 

NOTE

 

• Green India, Clean India (Option 1): Not the theme of Digital India Week 2022; this phrase is more commonly associated with environmental/afforestation campaigns.

 

• India’s Digital Start ups (Option 2): Startups were a focus area highlighted during the event but this was not the official theme.

 

• From Global to local (Option 3): Not the theme of Digital India Week 2022; this is not an official campaign slogan used for this event.

question: “Kavach” system introduced by Indian Railways is a/an ______.
option_2: System to increase the speed of the trains
solution_text:
The correct answer is Automatic Train Protection System.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic Train Protection (ATP) system introduced by Indian Railways to prevent train collisions caused by human error, such as a driver overshooting a red signal. (कवच — स्वचालित ट्रेन सुरक्षा प्रणाली)

 

• It was developed by the Research Designs and Standards Organisation (RDSO) in collaboration with Indian vendors, and is classified as a Safety Integrity Level 4 (SIL-4) certified system.

 

• Kavach automatically applies brakes if the driver fails to control the train's speed as per speed restrictions, and also alerts the driver in case of poor visibility (e.g., fog).

 

• It also enables the exchange of information between locomotives to prevent two trains from occupying the same track/section, thereby averting head-on and rear-end collisions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kavach was formerly known as the Train Collision Avoidance System (TCAS).

 

• Indian Railways aims to progressively expand Kavach coverage across high-density and high-speed routes.

 

NOTE

 

• Insurance scheme for passengers (Option 1): Kavach is a technological safety system, not a passenger insurance scheme.

 

• System to increase the speed of the trains (Option 2): Kavach's primary purpose is collision prevention and safety, not increasing train speed, though it does support safer higher-speed operations.

 

• Automatic crossing system (Option 4): Kavach is not specifically an automatic level-crossing gate system; it is a broader anti-collision/train protection system.

question: Who is the author of the book ‘The 7 Sins of Being a Mother’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tahira Kashyap Khurrana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ‘The 7 Sins of Being a Mother’ is a book authored by Tahira Kashyap Khurrana, an Indian author, filmmaker, and actor. (तहिरा कश्यप खुराना — लेखिका)

 

• The book explores the complexities, guilt, and challenges of modern motherhood in a candid and humorous manner.

 

• Tahira Kashyap Khurrana is married to actor Ayushmann Khurrana and has also directed short films and written other books, including ‘6 Degrees of Separation’ and ‘Souled Out’.

 

• She has been vocal about her personal journey, including surviving breast cancer, which she has written about in her work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Twinkle Khanna (Option 1) is also a well-known author, but of different books such as ‘Mrs Funnybones’ and ‘The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad’.

 

• Tahira Kashyap Khurrana has been recognised for her writing on themes of motherhood, body image, and cancer survivorship.

 

NOTE

 

• Twinkle Khanna (Option 1): Indian author and former actress known for books like ‘Mrs Funnybones’ and ‘Pyjamas Are Forgiving’, but not the author of this particular book.

 

• Alia Bhatt (Option 3): A well-known Bollywood actress, not an author of this book.

 

• Kareena Kapoor (Option 4): A Bollywood actress who has written books on pregnancy (e.g., ‘Kareena Kapoor Khan’s Pregnancy Bible’), but not the author of ‘The 7 Sins of Being a Mother’.

question:
Which of the following pair of country – name of grassland is correct?
I. Argentina – Pampas
II. Brazil – Steppe
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement I — Argentina – Pampas: This pairing is correct. The Pampas are temperate grasslands located in Argentina (also extending into Uruguay), known for cattle ranching and wheat cultivation. (पम्पास — अर्जेंटीना के घास के मैदान)

 

• Statement II — Brazil – Steppe: This pairing is incorrect. Steppe grasslands are found in the temperate regions of Eurasia, particularly Russia, Ukraine, and Central Asia, not in Brazil.

 

• Brazil's natural grassland/savanna regions are known as the Campos (temperate grassland) and Cerrado (tropical savanna), not Steppe.

 

• Since Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect, the answer is 'Only I'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous temperate grasslands include the Prairies (North America), Veld (South Africa), and Downs (Australia).

 

• The Pampas region is one of the world's most fertile agricultural areas and a major source of Argentina's beef and grain exports.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither I nor II (Option 1): Incorrect, since Statement I (Argentina – Pampas) is correct.

 

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, since Statement II (Brazil – Steppe) is the false pairing, not the correct one.

 

• Both I and II (Option 4): Incorrect, since Statement II incorrectly pairs Brazil with Steppe grassland.

question: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Kanauj in the year ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1540.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sher Khan (Sher Shah Suri) decisively defeated the Mughal emperor Humayun at the Battle of Kanauj (also called the Battle of Bilgram) in 1540. (शेरशाह सूरी — कनौज के युद्ध में हुमायूं को हराया, 1540)

 

• This defeat forced Humayun into a 15-year exile, during which he sought refuge in Persia (Iran) under the Safavid ruler Shah Tahmasp.

 

• Following this victory, Sher Shah Suri established the Sur Empire and became one of the most efficient administrators in medieval Indian history, known for reforms in revenue, currency (the Rupiya), and the Grand Trunk Road.

 

• Humayun eventually regained the Mughal throne in 1555, but died shortly after in 1556.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first major clash between Sher Khan and Humayun was the Battle of Chausa (1539), which Sher Khan also won.

 

• Sher Shah Suri's administrative reforms significantly influenced later Mughal administration, especially under Akbar.

 

NOTE

 

• 1555 (Option 2): This is the year Humayun recaptured Delhi and the Mughal throne, not the year of his defeat at Kanauj.

 

• 1535 (Option 3): Not associated with the Battle of Kanauj; this period saw Humayun's campaigns against Gujarat's Bahadur Shah.

 

• 1530 (Option 4): The year Humayun ascended the Mughal throne after Babur's death, not the year of the Battle of Kanauj.

question: Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra River in which of the following states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Majuli is a river island situated in the Brahmaputra River in the state of Assam, and is recognised as the world's largest river island. (माजुली — असम का नदी द्वीप)

 

• In 2016, Majuli became the first island in India to be made a separate district.

 

• It is an important centre of Assamese Vaishnavite culture, home to numerous satras (Vaishnav monasteries) established by the saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev.

 

• The island faces significant erosion from the Brahmaputra River, causing its area to shrink considerably over the decades.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Majuli has been in contention for inclusion on UNESCO's World Heritage Site tentative list.

 

• The island is also known for mask-making traditions and pottery crafted by its indigenous Mishing tribal communities.

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 1): Located in India's northeast, but Majuli is not situated in this state.

 

• Sikkim (Option 2): A Himalayan state in northeast India, not the location of Majuli island.

 

• Manipur (Option 3): Another northeastern Indian state, known for Loktak Lake, but not the location of Majuli.

question: Who among the following started the Kuka Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satguru Ram Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kuka Movement (also known as the Namdhari Movement) was started/organised as a religious and political reform movement by Satguru Ram Singh (Baba Ram Singh) in Punjab in 1857. (कूका आंदोलन — सतगुरु राम सिंह)

 

• It began as a movement for religious and social reform within Sikhism (opposing idol worship and caste discrimination, and advocating simple living), but evolved into one of the earliest movements with anti-British, non-cooperation elements, including a boycott of British goods, courts, and services.

 

• The British colonial government, alarmed by its growing influence, deported Baba Ram Singh to Rangoon (Burma) in 1872, where he died in exile in 1885.

 

• The Kukas (Namdharis) also strongly advocated cow protection, which brought them into direct conflict with British authorities, notably around the Amritsar and Malerkotla incidents of 1871–72.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kuka Movement is often cited as a precursor to the Non-Cooperation Movement, as it employed similar boycott tactics decades before Mahatma Gandhi.

 

• The Namdhari sect continues to exist today, tracing its spiritual lineage to Satguru Ram Singh.

 

NOTE

 

• Thakur Singh Sandhawalia (Option 1): A Sikh aristocrat associated with the Singh Sabha movement, not the founder of the Kuka Movement.

 

• Baba Dayal Das (Option 2): Founder of the Nirankari movement, a separate Sikh reform movement, not the Kuka Movement.

 

• Balak Singh (Option 3): An earlier spiritual guide of the Namdhari (Kuka) tradition who influenced Ram Singh, but it was Satguru Ram Singh who is credited with formally starting and organising the Kuka Movement as a mass movement.

question: Which of the following factors of soil formation determines the accumulation of the soil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Relief.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Relief (topography) is a key factor of soil formation that determines the accumulation of soil at a given location. (उच्चावच — मिट्टी के संचयन को निर्धारित करने वाला कारक)

 

• On steep slopes, soil formed by weathering is quickly washed/eroded away, so little or no soil accumulates there — such areas tend to have thin, immature soils.

 

• On flat or gently sloping land (plains, valleys, basins), weathered material tends to stay in place and accumulate over time, forming deep, mature soil profiles.

 

• Other factors of soil formation — parent rock, climate, and living organisms (flora and fauna) — influence soil's mineral composition, texture, and organic content, but relief specifically governs whether the weathered material stays and accumulates or is removed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The classical factors of soil formation are: parent material, climate, relief, organisms (biota), and time — often remembered by the acronym CLORPT.

 

• Soils formed on steep slopes are often classified as immature/skeletal soils due to continuous erosion preventing profile development.

 

NOTE

 

• Fauna (Option 1): Animal life (e.g., earthworms, burrowing organisms) contributes to soil aeration and mixing of organic matter, but does not determine accumulation.

 

• Flora (Option 2): Plant life contributes organic matter (humus) and influences soil fertility, but is not the primary determinant of soil accumulation.

 

• Parent rock (Option 4): Determines the mineral composition and initial texture of the soil, but not whether the soil accumulates or is eroded away — that is governed by relief.

question: What is the total number of medals won by India in 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won a total of 7 medals at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held in 2021) — its best-ever performance at a single Olympic Games. (टोक्यो ओलंपिक 2020 — भारत के कुल 7 पदक)

 

• The medal tally comprised 1 Gold, 2 Silver, and 4 Bronze medals.

 

• Neeraj Chopra won India's lone Gold medal in the Javelin Throw, becoming only the second individual Olympic gold medallist for India (after Abhinav Bindra in 2008) and the first in athletics.

 

• The remaining medals came from Mirabai Chanu (Silver, weightlifting), Ravi Kumar Dahiya (Silver, wrestling), PV Sindhu (Bronze, badminton), Lovlina Borgohain (Bronze, boxing), the Indian men's hockey team (Bronze), and Bajrang Punia (Bronze, wrestling).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's previous best was 6 medals at the London 2012 Olympics.

 

• The Indian men's hockey team's bronze at Tokyo 2020 ended a 41-year Olympic medal drought in hockey.

 

NOTE

 

• 6 (Option 1): This was India's medal tally at the London 2012 Olympics, not Tokyo 2020.

 

• 10 (Option 2): India has never won 10 medals in a single Olympic Games as of the exam date.

 

• 8 (Option 3): Not the actual medal count; India won 7 medals at Tokyo 2020.

question: Which of the following shortcut key is used add a new blank slide to an existing presentation of MS-PowerPoint 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ctrl + M.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-PowerPoint 365, the shortcut key Ctrl + M is used to insert a new blank slide into an existing presentation. (Ctrl + M — नई स्लाइड जोड़ने की शॉर्टकट कुंजी)

 

• The new slide is typically added immediately after the currently selected slide, using the same layout as the previous slide (or a default layout).

 

• This shortcut works consistently across various versions of PowerPoint, including desktop and Microsoft 365 versions.

 

• Other common PowerPoint shortcuts include Ctrl + N (create a new presentation file) and F5 (start the slideshow from the beginning).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ctrl + D in PowerPoint duplicates the selected slide or object.

 

• Shift + F5 starts the slideshow from the current slide rather than from the beginning.

 

NOTE

 

• Ctrl + N (Option 1): Used to create a new blank presentation (a new file), not a new slide within an existing presentation.

 

• Ctrl + Alt + M (Option 2): Not a standard PowerPoint shortcut for inserting a new slide; in some Microsoft Office applications, Ctrl+Alt+M is used to insert a new comment.

 

• Ctrl + Alt + N (Option 4): Not a standard shortcut associated with adding a new slide in PowerPoint.
